title: PRD (2025): Cohort-driven evaluation harness, graduated A/B gates, and staged failover for Optimize
author: Aisha Patel
body:
## Summary
This PRD defines a production-ready evaluation harness for Optimize that:
1) uses cohort-driven and sentinel prompt sampling,
2) gates A/B rollouts with statistical + business thresholds, and
3) implements a staged rollback/failover policy that escalates from automated throttles to cohort-level reverts to full rollback.

The goal is to reduce undetected regressions while keeping rollout velocity high for model and configuration updates.

## Background / Problem
We have recurring incidents where model/config rollouts pass coarse checks but produce regressions in specific customer cohorts or long-tail prompts. Current canaries are per-model and global; they miss cohort-specific quality regressions and provide coarse binary pass/fail decisions.

Optimize needs a more granular, actionable evaluation contract that ties observable signals to deterministic remediation steps and human-in-the-loop (HIL) triage when necessary.

## Goals
- Detect cohort-specific degradation with >90% recall for regressions causing >5% change in a business-impact metric.
- Prevent silent regressions via sentinel prompt detection and progressive gating across traffic slices.
- Reduce mean time to mitigation (MTTM) to under 20 minutes for high-severity regressions via deterministic rollback actions.
- Enable safe rapid rollouts with objective pass criteria at each stage.

## Non-goals
- Improve underlying model training processes (this is a serving/eval policy change).
- Replace manual post-deploy human QA for complex policy/regulatory cases.
- Provide full auto-rollback for noisy low-signal metrics without human review.

## Scope and Definitions
### Cohorts (v1 taxonomy)
Cohorts are deterministically assigned at request time using request metadata + customer/account attributes. The v1 taxonomy is:
- Persona: developer, analyst, support-agent
- Region: NA, EU, APAC
- Flow: latency-sensitive, long-context, tool-calling, regulatory
- Customer tier: top-enterprise, enterprise, growth, self-serve

### Blocked cohorts (require HIL approval to ramp beyond 5%)
Finalized list for v1:
- EU-regulated flows (all tiers)
- Top-10 enterprise customers (account list maintained by Customer Success; synced daily)

## Requirements
1) Sentinel prompt library
- Maintain a versioned library of sentinel prompts organized by cohort (persona/region/flow/tier).
- Include safety sentinels, reliability sentinels (tool-calling), and business-value sentinels (retention-sensitive / conversion proxies).

2) Cohort labeling and bucketing
- Deterministic bucketing at request time with a stable cohort key.
- Cohort labels must be available in evaluation events and rollout decisions.

3) Evaluation pipeline
- Compute per-cohort metrics in near-real-time with a maximum 3 minute lag (updated from 5 minutes based on SRE sizing and on-call usability).
- Support both online sampling (production traffic) and controlled replay (sentinel runs).

4) Graduated A/B gates in Console
- Gate rule configuration includes: minimum sample size, minimum detectable effect (MDE), alpha/beta, max allowed regression, and sustained-duration requirements.
- Default statistical method updated: sequential testing is the default for low-to-mid traffic cohorts; fixed-horizon remains available.

5) Staged rollback / failover engine
- Actions include: throttling new variant traffic, cohort-level divert to previous stable variant, full rollback.
- Each action is tied to explicit triggers and produces an auditable event in the release timeline.

6) Human-in-the-loop (HIL)
- HIL holds are required for blocked cohorts past 5% ramp.
- HIL is required for ambiguous composite detector states.
- Reviewer SLO: 30 minutes for P1 releases.

7) Surfacing and alerts
- Expose evaluation results and runbook links in Console release UI.
- Alert integration for Slack + PagerDuty with cohort breakdown and recommended action.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Sentinel library: >= 650 prompts covering at least 10 predefined cohorts, versioned and attributable (updated from 500/8 based on Evals team coverage plan).
- Per-cohort metrics computed and stored with <= 3 minute latency.
- Gate config defaults:
  - alpha = 0.05
  - beta = 0.2
  - sequential mode enabled by default for cohorts with < 50k daily requests
- Minimum sample size calculator present in UI and enforced for gate validity.
- Automated rollback triggers implemented (updated thresholds after SRE + Evals calibration in staging):
  - (a) Immediate throttle if any safety sentinel shows > 0.3% absolute regression sustained for 5 minutes.
  - (b) Automatic cohort-level divert to previous stable variant if composite quality score drops > 3% sustained for 10 minutes in that cohort.
  - (c) Full rollback if business KPI regression > 4% sustained for 10 minutes (updated from 5% for 5 minutes to reduce false negatives while avoiding brief KPI noise).
- Console includes a playbook link for each trigger with owner, checklist, and comms templates.
- End-to-end test harness can simulate cohorts and verify gating/rollback behavior in staging.

## Rollout Strategy
Phases and traffic slices (updated ramp plan to reduce step-size risk for large enterprise cohorts):
- Phase 0: Staging validation with synthetic traffic (2 weeks)
- Phase 1: Internal canary (0.5%) for 48 hours
- Phase 2: Beta customers (2%) for 72 hours
- Phase 3: Gradual ramp (10% for 24 hours, 25% for 24 hours, then 100% if gates pass)

Rules:
- Each phase requires passing cohort-specific gates.
- If any cohort fails a gate, apply automated action per remediation playbook and pause the release pending investigation.
- Blocked cohorts cannot ramp beyond 5% without explicit HIL approval in Console.

## Statistical Approach
### Defaults
- Binary signals (e.g., sentinel hit rate): two-sided proportion test.
- Continuous scores (e.g., composite quality): Welch’s t-test.
- Default alpha = 0.05, beta = 0.2.

### Sequential testing (default for low-to-mid traffic cohorts)
For cohorts with limited traffic, use sequential analysis with alpha spending (Pocock-style boundary) to allow earlier decisions while controlling Type I error.

### Sample size and MDE
Console enforces a minimum sample size requirement. The UI provides an MDE and n estimator and records the assumed baseline used for the calculation.

## Remediation Playbook
- Level 1 (Transient noise)
  - Auto-throttle new release traffic by 30% immediately.
  - If signals persist for 10 minutes, increase throttle to 50%.
  - Notify on-call; continue observation for 15 minutes.
- Level 2 (Cohort regression)
  - Divert failed cohort traffic to previous stable variant.
  - Create a P1 investigation ticket and open a dedicated War Room channel.
  - Require an explicit “resume” action with notes in Console.
- Level 3 (Business KPI impact)
  - Immediate full rollback of the release.
  - Notify via status page + account reps; schedule postmortem within 48 hours.
- Human-in-the-loop
  - For ambiguous composite detector states or blocked cohort ramps, move the release to HOLD.
  - Reviewers have a 30 minute SLO to approve/deny for P1 releases.

## Monitoring Signals
- Sentinel hit rate per cohort.
- Composite quality score per cohort (weighted accuracy proxy + hallucination penalty + latency penalty).
- Business KPIs: conversion rate, retention signal (as provided by customer integrations).
- Infrastructure: token cost variance, GPU latency P95, request error rate.
- Anomaly detectors: distribution drift (embedding distance) and abrupt change in output length.

## Console / UI Changes
- Release details page
  - Add a “Cohorts” tab: per-cohort metrics, sentinel breakdown, sample viewer.
  - Add a “Gates” panel: pass/fail status, confidence intervals, and sustained-duration progress.
- Gate configuration
  - Configure alpha/beta, fixed vs sequential mode, MDE, sustained-duration requirements, and mapped remediation actions.
- Notifications
  - Slack + PagerDuty wiring integrated into the release flow with cohort-aware routing.

## Data & Infra
- Storage for per-request metadata and evaluation events; retention updated to 180 days (from 90) to support quarter-over-quarter regressions and enterprise audit requests.
- Streaming pipeline to route sampled requests to evaluation workers (implementation depends on platform standard; initial deployment uses Kafka as in SRE sizing).
- Evaluation workers to run controlled prompts and compute metrics; require autoscaling profile and quotas.
- Dashboard endpoints and Console API to surface near-real-time cohort results.

## Timeline (updated)
- 2025-11-05: PRD created
- 2025-11-12: Design review & cohort taxonomy finalized
- 2025-11-20: API contract for gates approved
- 2025-11-28: Staging harness deployed
- 2025-12-06: Internal canary start
- 2025-12-12: Beta customers start (updated from earlier plan to allow extra staging burn-in)
- 2025-12-18: Target GA (updated from 2025-12-15 based on ramp plan and blocked cohort review bandwidth)

## Stakeholders
- Aisha Patel — PM (owner)
- Marco Li — Engineering (release engineering)
- Rina Gomez — Head of Evals
- Victor Chen — Console UX
- Sanjay Rao — SRE
- Priya Desai — Customer Success

## Open Questions
- What is the acceptable latency tradeoff for running sentinel prompts synchronously vs async for latency-sensitive flows?
- After-hours escalation owner for Level 2 cohort regressions (proposal: SRE primary with Evals secondary).
- Should Console surface raw model outputs for sampled requests, or only aggregated signals (compliance implications; default proposal: aggregated-only, with restricted break-glass access for on-call)?

## Change Log
- 2025-11-20: Initial PRD moved to in-review in Linear pending sign-off on alpha/beta defaults and blocked cohorts.
- 2025-12-03: Updated (a) evaluation lag target to <= 3 minutes, (b) sentinel library target to 650 prompts / 10 cohorts, (c) ramp steps to 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 100%, (d) rollback thresholds for safety and KPI signals, and (e) retention to 180 days.
